headlineRead: Weekend energy risk materially escalated. U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers after missile attacks on U.S. warships, while Iran warned shipping around Hormuz. Reuters reported Brent around $96.28 in the escalation. At the same time Iraq says export capacity is back above 3 million bpd and is pursuing Mediterranean pipeline routes, creating a second-order counter-theme: high prices are accelerating non-Hormuz rerouting. Equity markets are closed, so Friday stock prices and technical levels are carried forward rather than fabricated. No holding fundamental score or base idea conviction changes today.
whatsNewNow: U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Sep 5 after Iranian ballistic-missile attacks on U.S. Navy vessels; Iran then warned shipping and claimed retaliatory attacks. This shifts the conflict from general chokepoint disruption toward direct oil-transport risk.

Reuters reported Brent around $96.28/bbl during the escalation. U.S. Labor Day gasoline is expected around a record $4.03/gal and diesel remains near record levels, so refined products remain the stronger consumer/inflation channel.

Iraq says oil export capacity has recovered to above 3 million bpd and is pursuing northern/western Mediterranean routes. That is the clearest fresh counterweight to the Hormuz scarcity thesis and strengthens the long-run energy-rerouting theme.

TCS/HyperVault and partners announced up to roughly $7.4B for a 1GW AI data-centre campus in Telangana, another independent confirmation that AI infrastructure spending is broadening geographically and keeps power, switchgear, cooling and grid bottlenecks relevant.

TradingView Top Stories remain clustered around Tesla/Cybercab regulation, Nvidia/open-source AI, Snowflake AI monetisation, oil/yields and gold/yields; its current feed also surfaced Iraq's export-capacity recovery. TradingView remains discovery only and material claims were independently verified.
No new official ISM report exists since August Manufacturing 54.6 and Services 55.4; both were reverified and the ISM snapshot is not timestamp-churned.

Copper ex-US inventory tightness and input-cost transmission

Gold as structural hedge but tactically real-yield sensitive

developingThemes.name: Hormuz / Refined-Product Inflation + Direct Tanker Risk
developingThemes.whyNow: Direct U.S. strikes on three Iranian oil tankers and retaliatory Iranian shipping threats move the conflict into direct oil-transport risk.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Raises crude/product risk premium, gasoline/diesel/freight inflation, supports integrated/refining/shipping exposures and raises the probability of demand destruction/policy intervention.
developingThemes.confirmation: Further attacks, low Hormuz transit and persistent product tightness.
developingThemes.invalidation: Durable ceasefire plus normalization of tanker traffic and inventories.
developingThemes.nextTest: Sunday futures/Monday cash reaction, Hormuz traffic, EIA Sep 10, refinery outages.
developingThemes.action: Prefer quality integrated/refining/storage/logistics; no geopolitical chase.

developingThemes.name: Resilient Jobs/Services + Hot Inflation / Fed & Long-End Risk
developingThemes.whyNow: NFP +162k, unemployment 4.1%, Services PMI 55.4 and Services Prices 72.6 keep the growth/inflation mix too firm for easy policy relief.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Keeps real/nominal yields and funding hurdles high, favoring current cash flow and pricing power over leveraged duration.
developingThemes.confirmation: PPI/CPI stay sticky and yields remain elevated.
developingThemes.invalidation: Sharp disinflation and weaker labor without an earnings shock.
developingThemes.nextTest: Sep 10 PPI, Sep 11 CPI, Sep 15-16 FOMC.
developingThemes.action: Favor quality/cash conversion; avoid pre-commercial duration.

developingThemes.name: AI / Power / Transmission / Time-to-Power
developingThemes.whyNow: The new 1GW TCS/HyperVault campus extends the AI power buildout geographically while recent ISM comments continue to validate transmission/generation long-lead purchasing.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports grid equipment, contractors, switchgear, cooling, microgrids and generation independent of any single GPU cycle.
developingThemes.confirmation: Booked orders, customer deposits, named projects and FCF conversion keep rising.
developingThemes.invalidation: Funded project cancellations begin reducing supplier backlog.
developingThemes.nextTest: PWR/ETN/GEV/VRT orders and large-load interconnection screens.
developingThemes.action: Maintain quality leaders; valuation discipline remains mandatory.

developingThemes.name: Copper Ex-US Inventory Squeeze / Tariff Distortion
developingThemes.whyNow: Tariff-driven U.S. stockpiling continues to leave ex-US visible buffers thin while grid/electrification demand remains strong.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports miners but increases input pressure for cable, transformer and equipment names.
developingThemes.confirmation: LME/Shanghai inventories keep tightening and spreads stay firm.
developingThemes.invalidation: Tariff arbitrage unwinds and refined supply replenishes ex-US stocks.
developingThemes.action: FCX remains preferred near $70-72; do not chase squeeze pricing.

developingThemes.name: Energy Security Rerouting / Alternative Export Corridors
developingThemes.whyNow: Iraq says export capacity is back above 3 mbpd and is pursuing northern/western routes toward Mediterranean outlets, while non-Hormuz supply was already gaining importance.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Caps extreme Gulf scarcity over time, supports storage/pipeline/terminal/LNG infrastructure and can reshape regional crude differentials.
developingThemes.confirmation: Alternative pipeline/export capacity and long-term contracting continue rising.
developingThemes.invalidation: Hormuz normalizes quickly enough that expensive rerouting loses urgency.
developingThemes.nextTest: Iraq export volumes, Ceyhan/Banias pipeline milestones, Americas exports and LNG contracting.
developingThemes.action: Strengthen existing infrastructure/logistics research; no new ticker clears the bar today.

developingThemes.name: AI Funded-Load Quality + Capital Competition
developingThemes.whyNow: The buildout is broadening, but high funding costs keep deposits, named customers and cash conversion essential.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Rewards funded backlog and penalizes speculative interconnection queues/pre-revenue developers.
developingThemes.confirmation: Utilities keep enforcing deposits and suppliers retain order quality.
developingThemes.invalidation: Real yields collapse and speculative queues convert broadly to funded projects.
developingThemes.nextTest: Utility interconnection screens and AI infrastructure financing.

developingThemes.name: Food / Grain / Fertilizer Affordability
developingThemes.whyNow: Fuel/freight and Black Sea rerouting keep delivered food costs high, but input demand remains elastic by category.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Nitrogen/premium genetics are harder to defer; potash/phosphate and crop protection more deferrable; irrigation/machinery remain capex-cyclical.
developingThemes.confirmation: Crop/input ratios improve and application stays resilient.
developingThemes.invalidation: Grain/freight normalize while farm margins remain weak.
developingThemes.nextTest: Crop/input ratios, wheat exports, application rates and machinery orders.
developingThemes.action: BG/CTVA/CF quality preferred; AGCO still second-stage.

developingThemes.name: Selective AI Software / Cybersecurity Monetisation

developingThemes.confirmation: AI products expand ARR/RPO/FCF across multiple vendors.
developingThemes.invalidation: Growth slows while multiples remain elevated.
